subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>; procurement@acme.com
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — Acme Corp

Thanks again for a constructive call today — great to meet the Acme team. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned: 

Recap of use case:
- Primary workloads: customer-facing chat + downstream summarization for support cases. Mix of short intent classifications and longer multi-turn generation.
- Target behavior: keep interactive p95 latency low (goal: <=250ms p95 for single-turn chat) while supporting peak traffic windows.

What we heard on the call (please confirm or correct):
- You're leaning toward Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) but evaluating Private VPC for compliance; hosted API was considered but rejected for predictable latency/data isolation.
- Traffic profile (rough): sustained baseline traffic with peak spikes — you mentioned morning spike windows (we'll ask for logs below).
- Key requirements: model family preference (open Llama-3 style), strong p95 latency, and ability to burst during marketing events.

Dedicated sizing specifics we need to finalize:
- GPU preference: H100 (80GB) vs A100 (40/80GB) — H100 recommended for highest throughput, A100 can be cost-effective for less aggressive token budgets.
- TPS / concurrency targets: please provide sustained TPS, peak TPS, and concurrent requests during peak.
- Token mix: percent short/medium/long (example categories: <64 tokens, 64–256, >256), and average generated tokens per request.
- Sequence lengths: typical prompt length and response length distributions (we'll use these for KV cache and batch sizing).
- Latency SLOs: target p50/p95, and whether p99 matters for routing.

Preliminary ask from our side (attachments): I attached a short capacity worksheet (acme_capacity_sheet.pdf) — please fill the traffic columns and return. The SOW draft is attached to show lead time and onboarding tasks.

Next steps / proposed schedule:
1) Jordan / Acme: share a 48-hour traffic sample (logs or summary) and the filled capacity worksheet.
2) We'll schedule a 60-min sizing call with Rafael (solutions engineering) to walk through preliminary numbers and recommend GPU count/config. Rafael — can you run a quick back-of-the-envelope estimate once we have the traffic sample?
3) If Dedicated is confirmed, we'll propose a canary configuration for the first 30 days and sizing for steady state + burst buffer.

If you prefer, we can also include a short benchmark run on your representative prompts to validate latency.

Thanks — looking forward to the worksheet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and the numbers you asked for below.

Quick clarifications: we are leaning toward Dedicated for the predictable latency and isolation. Private VPC is an option but would be later in the procurement cycle (more of a compliance/legal conversation).

Traffic + token mix (current best estimates):
- Sustained TPS: ~12 TPS (typical weekday)
- Peak TPS: ~45 TPS (during morning spike + a daily digest push)
- Concurrency during peak: ~60 concurrent requests
- Token mix (by request count): 70% short (<64 tokens), 25% medium (64-256 tokens), 5% long (>256 tokens)
- Average generated tokens per call (weighted): ~220 tokens
- Typical prompt length: 30-80 tokens

Latency: our product team wants p95 <= 250ms for interactive flows; p99 is less critical but helpful for troubleshooting.

Procurement timeline: we are targeting a PO/commit by end of August if sizing and price look reasonable. For the call, I'm available Friday 23 Jul between 9–11am PT or Monday 26 Jul after 1pm PT.

I've attached a short CSV export from our observability that shows a representative day — I'll send the full 48-hour logs via the secure share after a quick scrub.

On the capacity worksheet: will start filling and return by Wednesday.

Thanks — Jordan

Hi Jordan / Marissa — thanks for the numbers, Jordan. Quick initial guidance based on the traffic & token mix you provided: 

Preliminary sizing notes (back-of-envelope):
- Given 45 TPS peak with ~220 average generated tokens and a 70/25/5 token distribution, the workload is medium-to-high token-budget. For interactive p95 <= 250ms we typically recommend H100 (80GB) class instances for best throughput headroom. A100 80GB is possible but will require more nodes and careful batching/quantization.

- Rough estimate: for your peak of 45 TPS using a Llama-3 style 70B-ish model (quantized), we'd start with a minimum of 3x H100 (80GB) nodes with concurrency shaping (32 concurrent slots per node) and autoscale config to 5x H100 for burst periods.
  - This nominal config assumes prefix/KV caching for repeated context and continuous batching tuned to your latency SLO.
  - If you prefer A100 to reduce cost, plan for ~5x A100 80GB equivalents and tighter batching to hit the same latency.

- Concurrency & batching: set per-node concurrency around 24–32 for low tail latency; continuous batching windows ~5–15ms works well for mixed short/medium requests.

- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for common customer prompts — this can reduce token compute substantially for repeated patterns and lower required node counts.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Once we have the 48-hour logs and the filled worksheet, I'll run a quick internal bench to produce a latency/throughput table for H100 vs A100 and a recommended autoscale policy.
2) We can run a short 2-hour benchmark on a representative subset of your prompts (no production traffic required) — that'll give a more precise node count and expected cost.
3) We'll draft an initial Dedicated config and show cost/latency trade-offs — then we can iterate toward a 30-day canary.

Would Friday 23 Jul 9:30am PT work for a 60-min sizing call? I can come prepared with a table comparing 3xH100 vs 5xA100 and expected p95 numbers.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
